Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: Localized, minimally tender, mildly warm swelling over left olecranon with preserved range of motion; no systemic symptoms; first episode; no trauma recalled.  
- Working diagnosis: Aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis.  
- Consistent differentials (from DDx):  
  • Septic olecranon bursitis—needs exclusion (medium likelihood);  
  • Gouty olecranon bursitis—consider (medium-low likelihood).  
- Management priorities: Reduce inflammation, rule out infection or crystal arthropathy, monitor for red-flag progression.

Management Plan

- Pharmacologic: Start Ibuprofen 400 mg PO twice daily after food for anti-inflammatory effect; discontinue if heartburn occurs.  
- Diagnostics: Blood test pack to be mailed; patient to attend phlebotomy for CBC, ESR/CRP, rheumatologic antibodies, serum urate.  
- Follow-up: Arrange review (video or face-to-face) approximately 6 days after blood draw to reassess elbow and discuss results.  
- Safety-netting: Seek urgent care if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, or systemic symptoms develop (possible septic arthritis).  
- Patient education: Explanation of bursitis, expected course, NSAID use, and warning signs provided.  

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis – High likelihood: Acute painless swelling, mild warmth, preserved function, no systemic illness.  
2. Septic olecranon bursitis – Moderate likelihood: Warmth and tenderness warrant exclusion despite lack of redness or fever.  
3. Gouty olecranon bursitis – Low-moderate likelihood: Age/sex risk; testing serum urate.
